title: Prefix-affinity epochal reclamation: deterministic eviction with prefix pinning and compact reclamation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The KV cache on GPU faces three correlated correctness/economics challenges: (1) prefix collisions and mis-eviction across batched requests, (2) unpredictable GPU memory fragmentation leading to failed allocations under bursty continuous batching, and (3) TTL-only or plain LRU strategies causing prefix-level inconsistency when prefixes are rehydrated concurrently by multiple requesters. Goal: Design and implement a deterministic eviction scheme that combines prefix-affinity buckets, short epoch leases (pin windows), and compact reclamation to keep correctness invariants (no stale prefix reads, monotonic KV lifetimes per prefix) while improving memory reclaim predictability and tail-latency under continuous batching.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction algorithm deployed behind feature flag: 'epochal-prefix-reclaim'
No prefix key returned after eviction: end-to-end test proves 0 stale-read regressions in fuzz trials (500k requests)
Tail latency (p95 generation) does not regress >5% under the flagged policy in the synthetic continuous-batching benchmark
GPU OOMs attributable to cache fragmentation reduced by >=60% in stress tests with mixed sequence lengths
A production canary rollout plan and a rollback path documented in the PR and Console runbook
design_decisions: Use prefix-affinity buckets: map prefixes to deterministic bucket IDs so eviction happens at bucket granularity to avoid splitting interdependent KV chains
Epoch leases: when a prefix is hot, assign a short lease (50-200ms) preventing eviction; leases are epoch counters incremented on major state transitions to avoid ABA problems
Demotion vs eviction: introduce a two-phase demotion where entries move from HOT -> WARM -> COLD before physical reclamation to reduce rehydration churn
Compact reclamation: perform compaction-aware free list merging per GPU slab to reduce fragmentation when reclaiming COLD buckets
Continuous-batching awareness: coordinate with the batching layer to 'soft-reserve' slab space for in-flight KV growth to avoid mid-batch OOMs
Linearizability goal scope: guarantee prefix-level monotonicity and non-staleness for in-flight request visibility; we do not aim for full cross-prefix linearizability in this iteration
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Simulation harness - model buckets, leases, demotion rules and slab fragmentation in the existing fuzzbench (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Runtime prototype - add bucket mapping, epoch counters, and demotion state machine in local dev builds; add feature flag gating (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Integration - hook compact reclamation into GPU allocator and batch coordinator, run microbenchmarks (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Canary - deploy to canary cluster with 5% traffic and enhanced tracing; monitor correctness metrics and latency (1 week)
Phase 5: Rollout - staged ramp with automated rollback on correctness or latency alerts
test_plan: Unit: epoch counter transitions, lease expiry, and bucket remapping logic
Fuzz: random concurrent rehydration + eviction traces (500k traces) to assert no stale reads
Stress: mixed-sequence-length continuous-batching workload at 3x production QPS for 2 hours to measure fragmentation and OOMs
Canary telemetry validation: assert p99/p95, rehydration counts, stale-read counters remain below thresholds
Chaos: simulate slow GPU allocator and transient kernel failures to verify graceful demotion and fallback
monitoring_and_signals: New metrics: prefix_lease_hits, prefix_lease_evictions, bucket_compactions, false_evictions_per_minute
Tracing: attach prefix_id to request traces to correlate rehydration events and batch boundaries
rollout_and_mitigation: Deploy feature-flagged implementation to canary cluster (5% traffic)
If stale-read counter > 0 (any), immediately disable flag and perform rollback; investigate logs with epoch traces
If p95 latency increases >5% for 10 minutes, reduce canary traffic to 1% and iterate on demotion timers
Fallback: revert to existing LRU-ttl policy (runtime-1.24) which has known properties and metrics
open_questions: Lease duration tuning: initial default 100ms — should this be adaptive based on prefix QPS?
Bucket sizing: static 256 buckets per shard vs dynamic split on heavy prefixes
Cross-tenant fairness: how aggressively should we reclaim tenant-dedicated buckets in multi-tenant Dedicated clusters?
Interaction with disk-backed cold-store (future): how to evict to disk vs GPU memory atomically
notes: Prototype simulations show 45% fewer allocation failures vs baseline LRU under synthetic heavy-tail sequence length mix
Compact reclamation added 8% CPU overhead on reclaim paths in microbench; need to measure end-to-end cost
This iteration focuses on correctness and fragmentation reduction; extra optimizations (adaptive lease, predictive pinning) are follow-ups
